nitrogenous wastes.

Even in the absence of hyperparathyroidism, hypophosphate-
mia occurs in as many as 50% of posttransplant patients.62 Th is 
is common due to renal tubular phosphate wasting and in-
creased urinary phosphate loss from the eﬀ ects of immunosup-
pressive medications. Most posttransplant patients will need 
to increase their phosphorus. Phosphorus supplementation is
often needed in the early posttransplant period. Serum potas-
sium levels should be monitored closely, because some phos-
phorus supplements (Neutraphos-K) contain large amounts of 
potassium.
